paras: The mob attack on Dock Thomas was an assault in Chicago, reported in August 1900, in which a crowd of nearly a hundred men and boys chased Thomas, a Black Pullman car porter, off a dock into the lake and stoned him in the water. Police arrived before he was seriously injured, and the only report found said the crowd would probably have stoned him to death without them.

According to the report, Thomas and another Black man had been fishing from the dock when they fell into a quarrel. The two men threw stones at each other, and one of the stones struck a woman on the head.

A crowd then ran after Thomas, yelling "kill him," and forced him off the dock into the water. Once he was in the lake, "a perfect hail of stones" fell around him. Police reached the scene before he was seriously hurt, and the attack ended.
The report names no member of the crowd and mentions no arrests or charges, either against the attackers or against the men in the quarrel.

The episode is known from a single short item, headlined "Rescued by Police," printed without a dateline on page 2 of the Neihart Herald, a Montana weekly, on August 11, 1900. The item called the crowd "infuriated" and credited the "timely arrival of the police" with saving Thomas, but it gave no date for the incident and no race for the crowd. No Chicago account, no other white-press report and no Black-press coverage of the attack was found.
